Ivy Chen: Hey team, first-week snag. I can connect to the internet but `ssh bastion.corp.redwood` fails with "could not resolve hostname". Okta shows connected. I'm on Fedora Silverblue with Firefox DoH enabled. Any tips?
Diego Alvarez: welcome Ivy! quick Qs: does `dig bastion.corp.redwood` return an internal IP locally? Also which resolver is in /etc/resolv.conf?
Ivy Chen: `dig bastion.corp.redwood` returns SERVFAIL from 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare) and my /etc/resolv.conf points to 127.0.0.53 (systemd-resolved).
Megan O.: ah that explains it. We use split-DNS for corp domains; Cloudflare/DoH bypasses the system resolver and can't see internal zones. Two options: 1) disable DoH in Firefox and re-open so the system resolver (which gets Okta-pushed DNS) is used, or 2) add a temporary /etc/hosts entry pointing bastion.corp.redwood -> 10.9.8.7 (ask infra for the IP).
Ivy Chen: How do I disable DoH quickly?
Megan O.: in Firefox: Settings > General > Network Settings > uncheck 'Enable DNS over HTTPS'. For a CLI test, `nmcli device show` should show DNS servers pushed by Okta (169.254.x.x). You can also `dig @169.254.12.1 bastion.corp.redwood` to test directly against the VPN DNS.
Ivy Chen: dug directly at the VPN DNS and got 10.9.8.7. Disabled DoH in Firefox, flushed systemd-resolved cache (`sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches`) and now `ssh ubuntu@bastion.corp.redwood` gives connection refused (progress!).
Diego Alvarez: progress = good. Connection refused means DNS+routing ok but either port 22 closed or your user/key mismatch. Check `ssh -v` and that your public key is attached to your profile. Also infra sometimes blocks SSH until corp-ssh-access IAM tag is approved. infra-bot can confirm.
infra-bot: Ivy Chen's IAM tag corp-ssh-access: pending approval. Please request infra review in #eng-infra to enable console SSM sessions and SSH tagging.
Ivy Chen: oh I didn't realize that step existed. Filing the infra request now. In meantime `ssh -v` shows permission denied (publickey). I uploaded my key to the profile and retried; now connected. Thanks!
Megan O.: great. Doc action: add a new-hire note: "If internal hostnames fail to resolve, check for DNS-over-HTTPS / DoT in browsers or system resolvers; test `dig @<VPN_DNS> <host>` and disable DoH if necessary. Fallback: add /etc/hosts entry until DNS/Okta policy is pushed."
Ivy Chen: will add to my onboarding checklist. tagging this thread for others: disable DoH or test against VPN DNS, then upload SSH key and request IAM tag. :tada:
